  * The `tinterval` function

## Some Things to Consider


#### Tidy your data!

* Make sure that your data is nice and clean. Common pitfalls (to avoid!) could be:
  * ID-variable has missing values
  * Missing values not consistengly coded as `NA` (e.g., `-99`)
  * Check distributions and stationarity with plots
  * No within-person variance for some cases (exclude those)

#### Start simple!

* Models fitted in a Bayesian framework (with MCMC) usually take much longer to fit than models fitted in a frequentist framework (e.g., with maximum likelihood)
  * However, most DSEM and related models are too complex for ML
  * Start with simple models, check convergence, and gradually increase complexity. When you finish running a complex model, save the fitted model object so you don't have to refit too often!
  

#### Beware: Your data gets saved while fitting!

:::: {.columns}

::: {.column width="58%"}

* Any fitted model object will contain the raw data. **If you do not wish to make the data publicly available** (as part of a fitted model object), run:

:::

::: {.column width="6%"}

:::

::: {.column width="36%"}

::: {.vspace}
:::



```{r}
#| echo: true
#| eval: false

fit$data <- NULL
```


:::
